Grounds and garden is built: the east passage gravel run is split at z 13..14 so it no longer writes into the chimney E footing; the part places 603 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette.
make.sh now runs to "build.nbt ready" with this part clean. The only change is in parts/garden.mjs (one pathRun split into two, with a comment).
Only the garden part was fixed; no other module was edited.</summary>
<parameter name="finished">true
left: Other parts still refuse writes, not in this part's scope: Chimneys, hearths and lights (2 writes at 7,26,30 and 8,26,30 against the chimney S cap); Keeper's aisle (12,11,17 and 12,12,17 against the shell's iron_chain/lantern); Wing kitchen and scullery (7,6,29 furnace vs smoker). make.sh still produces build.nbt despite these.

waste.what: Found the refused footing by reading the make.sh REFUSED line and then the report's (x,y,z) list, and worked out by hand that the gravel run at x 20..21 covers the chimney E footing z 13..14.
waste.cost: 2 make.sh runs, about 4 tool calls of inspection; the cell-by-cell check was done in my head.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`/`check` command that lists, for a part's pending writes, which earlier-part cells they hit and which footprint (chimney footing, floor, wall) owns the cell, before the build runs. It would also name the blocking part and its plan.md row.

waste.what: Split a path run by hand around a footing. pathRun has no way to skip a box, so I computed two segments ([20,6]-[20,12] and [20,15]-[20,21]) to keep the gravel out of the footing.
waste.cost: 1 edit, computed by hand from the width-2 centring rule (extra cell to +x).
waste.tool: A `skip` / `avoid` box option on pathRun and the other surface helpers (or a `reserved` set taken from the earlier parts), so a long edge run stops at a footing without the author splitting it into segments.

waste.what: parts-report.json lists refusals with coordinates but nothing about the owner of the cell (which earlier part and which plan row placed it), so tracing each one meant reading the other parts' code.
waste.cost: about 3 greps and reads across vocab/h2.mjs and the report; repeated for the other parts' refusals.
waste.tool: runParts could write, for each refusal, the owning part's name and the plan.md element that claimed the cell into the report.
